questions.q: What will the son learn if he listens carefully to what he should understand?
questions.a: If he listens carefully to what he should understand, the son will learn to be able to choose wisely what to do, and to know the right things to say.

questions.q: What will happen to you after being with an adulteress woman?
questions.a: After being with such a woman you will be miserable, as if you had eaten a bitter plant.

questions.q: To where are such a woman’s feet going?
questions.a: Her feet are going down to death.

questions.q: What advice does the father give the sons about getting near any adulterous woman?
questions.a: The sons are to keep far away from any adulterous woman and not even go near her house.

questions.q: What will the son give away if he goes to such a woman?
questions.a: If he goes to such a woman, the son will give away the best efforts of his youth.

questions.q: What will happen at the end of his life if the son becomes involved with an adulterous woman?
questions.a: If the son becomes involved with an adulterous woman, he will groan when he is about to die.

questions.q: What will the son say at the end of his life if he becomes involved with an adulterous woman?
questions.a: If he becomes involved with an adulterous woman, he will say that he hated correction and despised rebuke.

questions.q: From where should the sons drink?
questions.a: The sons should only drink water from their own well, which means to have sex with his wife only.

questions.q: With what should the a son be exhilarated?
questions.a: He should be exhilarated by how the wife of his youth loves him.

questions.q: Whom should the son enjoy sexually?
questions.a: The father tells the son to enjoy sexually the woman whom he married when he was young.
Yahweh knows everything that people do.

questions.q: What will capture and grasp the wicked person?
questions.a: The wicked things that the wicked one does will capture him and his sin will be like cords that grasp him.

commentary.text: Exhortations to wisdom. The evils of licentiousness.
Remedies against licentiousness, The miserable end of the wicked.

Verses 1–14 Solomon cautions all young men, as his children, to abstain from fleshly lusts. Some, by the adulterous woman, here understand idolatry, false doctrine, which tends to lead astray men's minds and manners; but the direct view is to warn against seventh-commandment sins. Often these have been, and still are, Satan's method of drawing men from the worship of God into false religion. Consider how fatal the consequences; how bitter the fruit! Take it any way, it wounds. It leads to the torments of hell. The direct tendency of this sin is to the destruction of body and soul. We must carefully avoid every thing which may be a step towards it. Those who would be kept from harm, must keep out of harm's way. If we thrust ourselves into temptation we mock God when we pray, Lead us not into temptation. How many mischiefs attend this sin! It blasts the reputation; it wastes time; it ruins the estate; it is destructive to health; it will fill the mind with horror. Though thou art merry now, yet sooner or later it will bring sorrow. The convinced sinner reproaches himself, and makes no excuse for his folly. By the frequent acts of sin, the habits of it become rooted and confirmed. By a miracle of mercy true repentance may prevent the dreadful consequences of such sins; but this is not often; far more die as they have lived. What can express the case of the self-ruined sinner in the eternal world, enduring the remorse of his conscience!

Lawful marriage is a means God has appointed to keep from these destructive vices. But we are not properly united, except as we attend to God's word, seeking his direction and blessing, and acting with affection. Ever remember, that though secret sins may escape the eyes of our fellow-creatures, yet a man's ways are before the eyes of the Lord, who not only sees, but ponders all his goings. Those who are so foolish as to choose the way of sin, are justly left of God to themselves, to go on in the way to destruction.
